newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia king warns of problems facing country.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia king warns of problems facing country.

text.p: Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk wants to draw attention to critical problems such as economic instability and deforestation before he steps down within two years, the king's palace said on Thursday.
Listing the problems of deforestation, "savage capitalism", factionalism, the decay of moral values and AIDS, Sihanouk concluded that Cambodia could head into a downward spiral.
"At the end of my life, I don't only have the right but also the duty to 'sound the alarm'," Sihanouk said.
Sihanouk, who is in Beijing undergoing medical treatment, was answering written questions from his cabinet. His responses were dated in early March but publicly released by the palace on Thursday.

Sihanouk, who recently said he was unhappy on the throne and expressed dismay over the state of Cambodia's coalition government, said he would abdicate within two years as within his constitutional rights.

"But now I am too old and sick to lead a futile struggle against those, meanly and unjustly, who set themselves up as my enemies. I will take my final retirement before one or two years," the king told his cabinet.
Sihanouk appeared to be reacting to comments by co-Premier Hun Sen, who has said abdication is not constitutional and warned Sihanouk against entering politics.
Hun Sen and Sihanouk's son, co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, formed a shaky coalition following U.N. polls in 1993 and have bitterly feuded over a range of issues.

In a series of four interviews, Sihanouk painted a portrait of Cambodia that bordered on apocalyptic. He worried that government infighting, gangsters, lawlessness and corruption threatened financial stability and could undo the country.
"Our Cambodia is forced, if it wants to survive, to proceed with a true...pure and tough revolution," he said.
